subject: Private deployment sizing & license model — Argus Health
messages:
From: Lauren Hunt <lauren@argushealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim Cohen <tim.cohen@argushealth.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment sizing & license model — Argus Health

Jonas — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from our side to make sure we're aligned and to flag the asks procurement will need: 

Summary of what we said on the call:
- Primary goal: host a private/VPC deployment for our clinical summarization pipeline with strict data residency (US-only).
- Expected steady-state token volume: ~18M–25M tokens/month (spikey around product launches, up to ~40M/month peak).
- Initial environment footprint: 3 environments (prod, staging, dev) across two teams; possibility to expand to 5 in year 1 depending on adoption.
- Performance needs: 100–150 concurrent requests at 256-token avg context, 200ms median tail desirable.
- Security: SOC2 + audit logs + KMS integration — essential for procurement.

Commercial/contract asks from procurement:
- Pricing model: prefer an annual license + per-1M token unit price. Target unit economics: ~$850 / 1M tokens (this is our procurement target to fit the internal budget).
- Budget range: $15k–$25k per month initially (we know this is a function of the final unit price and envs).
- Payment/terms: Net-60; need to confirm whether Redwood requires Net-30 or can accept Net-60 for enterprise agreements.
- SLA & support: require an enterprise support tier with a named TAM and 24x5 coverage.

Immediate asks: 
1) Can you provide a simple worksheet that maps license fee + $/1M token to total monthly cost across our stated token ranges and env counts?
2) Can you include support tier options and what they include (TAM, response times, included training)?
3) Please surface any minimum commitments you expect for Private/VPC deployments and whether burst/bandwidth is priced separately.

Attachments: I attached our internal product brief (argus-reqs-sow.pdf) for context.

Thanks — Lauren
Lauren Hunt
Director, Product Ops | Argus Health

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Hunt <lauren@argushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment sizing & license model — Argus Health

Lauren — great to sync, appreciated the clear rundown. I've attached a license worksheet that maps several common permutations (license-only, license + per-token unit, and a committed throughput slab) against the token ranges you listed. High-level responses to your asks below.

Answers / proposal highlights:
- Licensing model: Redwood typically structures Private/VPC deals as an annual platform fee (covers runtime, control plane, baseline ops) + a per-1M-token usage charge. For deals that need strict SLAs/TAM and private support, we layer an "Enterprise Support" add-on.
- Example ranges (ballpark): annual platform fee $30k–$75k depending on env count and deployment complexity; usage price typically $600–$900 / 1M tokens in the mid-market for Private deployments depending on commit and support tier. Committed volume discounts apply at >50M tokens/month.
- Support tiers: Standard (business hours, email), Premium (24x5, 2-hour P1), Enterprise (named TAM, 1-hour P1, quarterly reviews). We'll include explicit response-time SLAs in the quote.
- Minimum commitments: we recommend a 12-month minimum for Private to cover provisioning and support; no GPU-hour minimums beyond the committed throughput unless you elect burst capacity. Burst is priced as a short-term uplift; details in worksheet.

I've attached: redwood-license-worksheet.xlsx (worksheet with modeling tabs) and a preliminary quote PDF. I'll get legal to produce a starter MSA after we agree on target unit economics and commitment term. 

Next steps I propose:
- I'll circulate a tailored worksheet with three canonical options: (A) 3-env, 12-month, Moderate commit; (B) 5-env, 12-month, Higher commit; (C) 3-env + Enterprise support (shorter lead).
- Can you confirm which of those you want modeled first?
- I'll also validate Net-60 with finance, but we can typically make exceptions on enterprise deals pending procurement sign-off.

Attachments: redwood-license-worksheet.xlsx (calc tabs), preliminary-quote-ARG-4721.pdf

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0122

From: Tim Cohen <tim.cohen@argushealth.com>

Jonas / Lauren — looping in procurement and letting you know a few clarifications from our side: 

Procurement notes:
- We need the worksheet broken out as line-items to drop into our procurement system (license line, token usage line, support line, optional SOC2 evidence attachment).
- Payment: Argus requests Net-60 and a single consolidated invoice monthly.
- Environment ask: based on product requirements we've bumped the likely env count to 5 (prod x2 for active-active, staging, qa, dev) — please model 5-env option.
- Security: we'll need a SOC2 attestation + evidence of KMS/HSM integration before legal will sign.

Budget calibration from finance: expected starting monthly spend target to keep exec approval is $18k–$28k; hitting >$35k/month will need an additional exec review. That means your per-1M token price needs to be within that target when combined with the platform fee.

Please include an explicit example row: "Total monthly cost if we run 22M tokens/mo at X $/1M + Y platform fee". Also include an option with a 12-month commit and a higher commit (24-month) to show discounts.

Thanks — Tim Cohen
